chunks: Abul Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad al-Katib reported to me from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Za'farani, from Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi, from al-Mas'udi, from Muhammad ibn Kathir, from Yahya ibn Hammad al-Qattan, from Abu Muhammad al-Hadhrami, from Abu Ali al-Hamdani:

Abdul Rahman ibn Abu Layla called upon Amirul Mu'mineen Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him, and said: "O Amirul Mu'mineen! I want to ask you so as to learn from you, though we have waited for long to hear you say something about your matter, but you never said anything. Would you not tell us about this matter of yours — was it a covenant from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, or something you had opined? We have had a lot of sayings about you, and the most reliable for us is what we accepted from you and heard from your mouth. Indeed, we used to say: if the Caliphate were to return to you after the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, no one would have disputed with you in it. By Allah, I do not know what to say if I am asked! Should I claim that the people were more worthy than you in what they held? And if I say that, then for what purpose did the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant peace, appoint you after the Farewell Pilgrimage, when he said: 'O people, whoever I am his master, then Ali is his master.' And if you were worthier than them in what they held, then on what basis should we accept their authority?"

Amirul Mu'mineen, peace be upon him, said: "O Abdul Rahman, surely, when Allah, Most High, called back His Prophet, may God bless him, his family and grant peace, I was worthiest of all people for the authority, more than I am of this shirt of mine. And I had a covenant from the Prophet of God to me; even if you were to lead me by the nose, I would have submitted in obedience to God and submission. And the first thing that was taken from us after him was the invalidation of our right in the Khums. And when our position weakened, the herdsmen of cattle from Quraysh coveted us. And indeed I had a right upon the people; if they had returned it to me voluntarily, I would have accepted it and managed it, and it was for a stipulated term. And I was like a man who has a right upon the people until a term; if they paid him early his property, he took it and thanked them for it; and if they delayed it, he took it without them being thanked. And I was like a man accepting easy terms while he was, among the people, full of grief. And indeed the guidance is known by the fewness of those who accept it from the people. So when I am silent, excuse me; for indeed if there comes a matter in which you need a reply, I shall reply to you. So withhold from me what I have withheld from you."

Then Abdul Rahman said: "O Commander of the Faithful, you are, by your soul, just as the earlier poet said: 'By your soul, you have indeed awakened the one who was asleep, and you have caused the one with two ears to hear.'"

key_terms.الخُمُس: One-fifth tax on certain gains prescribed in the Quran (8:41), whose distribution is a right of the Prophet's family
key_terms.حَجَّة الوَداع: The Prophet's final pilgrimage to Mecca in 10 AH, during which he delivered several important declarations
key_terms.غَدِير خُمّ: The location where the Prophet (s) declared Ali (as) as mawla (master/guardian) of the believers during the Farewell Pilgrimage
key_terms.مَوْلى: Master, guardian, or patron; the key term in the Ghadir declaration establishing Ali's authority

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about his right to the caliphate when Abdul Rahman ibn Abu Layla questioned him?
ai.summary: Abdul Rahman ibn Abu Layla approaches Imam Ali (as) asking why he never spoke about his claim to the caliphate, questioning whether it was based on a covenant from the Prophet (s) or personal opinion. He references the Ghadir Khumm declaration. Imam Ali responds that he was indeed the most worthy successor but had a covenant with the Prophet to accept what befell him with patience. He explains how their right to Khums was first taken away, which weakened their position and emboldened the Quraysh. He uses the analogy of a creditor patiently waiting for a debt to be repaid.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 2. He said: Abul Hasan ‘Ali ibn Muhammad al-Katib reported to me from al-Hasan ibn ‘Ali al-Za’farani, who reported from Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi, who reported from al-Mas’oodi, who reported from Muhammad ibn Katheer, from Yahya ibn Hammad al-Qattan, who reported from Abu Muhammad al-Hadhrami, from Abu ‘Ali al-Hamdani,

that once Abdul Rahman ibn Abu Layla called upon Amirul Mu’mineen ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him and said: "O Amirul Mu’mineen! I want to ask you so as to learn from you, (though) we have waited (for long) to hear you say something about your matter, but you never said anything. Would you not tell us whether it was a covenant from the Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny, or was it something you had opined? We have had a lot of false sayings about you! However, we have found what we have to accept from you and what we have heard from your mouth is most reliable. Indeed, some of us say that if Caliphate were to return to you after the Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny, no one would have disputed with you. By Allah, I do not know what to reply if asked. Should I consider that the people who took over were more worthy than you? And if I say so, then for what purpose did the Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny, appoint you at the Farewell pilgrimage, when he said: ’O People, of whosoever I am the Master, ‘Ali is also his Master.’ So, if you were worthier for the authority than them, then on what score should we accept their authority?"

Amirul Mu’mineen, peace be upon him, said: "O Abdul Rahman, surely, when Allah, Most High, called back His Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny, I was worthiest of all people for the authority. But I had a covenant with the Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny, as a result of which I had to submit to the will of Allah even if they were to lead me by the nose. Surely, the first loss that was sustained was the invalidating of our right in Khums; and when our position was weakened, then the herdsmen of Quraish pounced upon us with greed. Thus, the people were indebted to us, and if they had voluntarily returned to me my rights, I would have accepted and managed it, even for a stipulated time. So I lived among them as a creditor, for a stipulated time. If they paid back earlier, the creditor would repossess his goods and thank them; and if they delayed it, he would take it without considering them deserving any gratitude. So, I was like a person accepting easy terms, yet living among them full of grief. The right guidance is identified by a small group of people who accept it. So when I am silent, excuse me. And if the time comes when you need my reply, I shall reply you. So withhold from me what I have withheld from you!"

Then Abdul Rahman said: "O Amirul Mu’mineen, by your soul, you are like the one of whom the earlier poet said: "By your soul, you have indeed awakened the one who was asleep and you have caused the one with two ears to hear."
